newsitem.title: USA: US, Japan business leaders seek stable dlr/yen rate.
newsitem.headline: US, Japan business leaders seek stable dlr/yen rate.

text.p: U.S. and Japanese business leaders called on Wednesday for steps to minimize a rise in the Japanese trade surplus and to stabilize the yen-dollar exchange rate within "an appropriate range."

More than 70 U.S. and Japanese business leaders said in a joint statement issued at the end of a two day meeting in San Francisco that a stable exchange rate that reflects the economic fundamentals of both the United States and Japan is "indispensable for the proper conduct of business."

"Therefore, efforts to improve economic fundamentals must continue so as to minimize the incipient rise in the Japanese trade-current account surplus, and thus to stabilize the yen-dollar exchange rate within an appropriate range reflecting basic fundamentals," the joint statement said.
The business leaders said that despite progress made in recent years, market access remained "a top priority." American business leaders have long sought greater access to the Japanese markets.
The statement said Japan's deregulation efforts must be accelerated "in its own interest to sustain economic growth."
